p2.use.1: Tap the striped or plain half circle to step colors forward or back in the same order as the penlight. Press it as many times as you press your real penlight to see which color is on and which members use it. The small circles show the previous and next colors. Use ⚙ to choose the live and penlight, and 🔒 to prevent mis-taps.
p2.use.3: The top side is for the common color vision player (self-reported), the bottom side for the color vision diversity player (self-reported). The bottom player matches the shown member's color, and the top player answers "Great!" or "So close!". Good for the wait before the show.

p2.offline: Open this page once before you go. It saves itself and works without signal. Add it to your home screen (iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen / Android: menu → Install app) to use it like an app.
p3.intro: The top side is the common color vision player (self-reported), the bottom side the color vision diversity player (self-reported). It is less about winning and more about learning how each other sees.
p3.fixedLayout: The half-circle layout is fixed in this game (edits from page 1 are not used).

p3.bottomRole: Match the color of the member shown

p5.mindset: You might not even have noticed that your oshi's color changed.
Penlights around you are free to be anything. They may not have the official colors.
Not knowing other members' colors is normal. Nobody can watch every stream and clip.
Sometimes an oshi asks for a color only in members-only streams.
People with color vision diversity see some colors differently from you, and they enjoy it positively, not sadly.
Even if the oshi button lets your top oshi slip out, they keep cheering with all their heart.
Some operate the penlight blind at god speed so they never miss a moment, and the buttons cannot keep up.
Your oshi has a heart strong enough to turn a wrong penlight color into a joke. No need to worry.
p5.quote: "Can't you guys just get along, seriously?"
p5.understood: With all that in mind, let's begin.

p5.hint: Pick the color with the penlight-style buttons, then press Decide. The light keeps its color for the next question. The fewest presses from the current color scores the most.

p14.items: Page 1 gets the oshi button (Hot Button) (set it in ⚙).
The lock button size on page 1 can be changed (in ⚙).
Surprise guest members can be shown or hidden (OFF by default).
Half-circle hit areas can be shown in color, with adjustable transparency.
Page 5 scores become "95 pts♠" (correct, fewest presses) / "67 pts" (correct, longer way) / "2 pts♠" (wrong), and "Got it!" shows your answer list.
Member images (the image column in the data) are shown on top of the penlight color, see-through.
Leaving the page or closing the app turns debug mode off again.
